back: Enthalpy change when one mole of a gaseous ion dissolves in enough water to give an infinitely dilute solution; always exothermic.
Enthalpy change when one mole of an ionic solid dissolves in enough water to give an infinitely dilute solution; either sign.
ΔHsol = −ΔHlatt + ΣΔHhyd (multiply each ion's ΔHhyd by its number in the formula).
Higher ionic charge and smaller radius (higher charge density) give more exothermic hydration.
δ− oxygen towards cations; δ+ hydrogen towards anions: ion-dipole attractions.

front: Why ΔHsol can be either sign
back: It is the small difference between two large terms: the lattice energy to be overcome and the hydration enthalpies released.

front: A salt whose dissolving is endothermic
back: Ammonium nitrate (used in cold packs) and potassium bromide: the solution cools.
